title: KV segmentation & granular reclamation protocol for reduced GPU fragmentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Overview: This ticket defines and implements a segmented KV allocation and granular reclamation protocol designed to limit long-term GPU memory fragmentation while preserving continuous batching throughput and KV cache hit rates. Motivation: Current KV allocation can produce micro-fragments that accumulate over time, forcing larger-than-needed evictions or full-region compactions that spike GC and increase tail latency. We need a strategy that allows fine-grained reclamation, low-overhead relocation, and compatibility with existing batching and caching heuristics.
design_summary: We propose dividing each KV pool into fixed-size microsegments (32KB - 256KB tunable) organized into hot/mid/cold rings. Allocation chooses the smallest segment size that fits the item (best-fit at segment granularity). When fragmentation is detected (free fraction below threshold on a ring or sustained allocation failures), a lightweight relocation pass is triggered that: 1) samples candidate live entries via probabilistic walker (bounded CPU/GPU work), 2) migrates chosen entries to compact destination segments using asynchronous copy + pointer indirection, 3) frees and merges now-empty segments returning them to the free ring. Relocation operates at segment level and avoids large monolithic compactions; it is rate-limited by a background budget tied to observed batching latency to prevent SLO regressions.
telemetry_and_metrics: Add/extend metrics: segment_count_by_bucket, avg_free_fragment_ratio, sample_relocation_success_rate, relocation_bytes_per_minute, eviction_retries_due_to_fragmentation, batch_latency_p50/p95_when_relocating. Expose a fragmented_segment_histogram and a per-model kv_fragment_score so product/ops can monitor drift. Create an alert if avg_free_fragment_ratio < 0.12 for 15m and eviction_retries_due_to_fragmentation > 10/min.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce avg free-fragment ratio (across production pools) by >=30% compared to baseline over a 7-day run without manual compaction
No >5% regression in p95 generation latency during steady-state and relocation background activity
Eviction-induced quality regressions (measured by token loss on representative evals) remain within current noise bands
Background relocation budget prevents CPU/GPU saturation and is automatically scaled down when batch latency increases >3%
End-to-end validated on staging with model mix: chat-16k, instruct-8k, quantized-7B and large sequence synthetic workload

risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Indirection adds one pointer chase on KV lookup which may slightly increase per-token overhead; mitigate by caching indirection hits for hot keys.
- Over-aggressive relocation could compete with batching and increase latency; mitigated via dynamic background budget tied to observed batch latencies.
- Complexity of multiple segment sizes increases allocator logic and testing surface.
- Hardware-specific memcpy/async copy primitives behave differently across GPU generations; need cross-hardware validation and graceful fallback to CPU-based relocation for failing devices.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-gate behind runtime flag. 2) Internal staging run for 72h with synthetic fragmentation and traffic mix; monitor metrics. 3) Canary to 5% of traffic on dedicated clusters with telemetry sampling. 4) Gradually increase to 25%, 50% while monitoring alerts and manual sanity checks. 5) Full rollout and deprecation of legacy compaction path after 4 weeks of stable metrics.
